svg.text: A tighter overview should push the work, not the chrome.
You have growth momentum, but the overview still needs to feel sharper and more deliberate.

The redesign direction here is a hard-edge command surface: square cards, square controls, sharper separators, and clearer content hierarchy. The main job of the page is to surface the next best actions without feeling soft or generic.
High-value pages are still pulling new traffic.
Internal linking is improving deeper page discovery.
Title fixes are the fastest next lever to pull.
Rankings are stronger, but page two still matters.
One ranked queue, not ten competing widgets.
This is the center of the redesign. Alerts, opportunities, and guidance collapse into one ranked work queue with impact and one clear next step per row.
fix low-CTR winners on two high-impression queries
refresh three landing pages slipping from positions 4-8
strengthen internal links for twelve page-two opportunities
The sharper direction is not just “less border radius.” It means tighter framing, more decisive rows, fewer decorative pills, and clearer rectangular structure across the whole dashboard.

Traffic is stable enough to support a focused sprint. The overview should feel like a command surface, not a glossy widget gallery. Keep the main decision at the top, put the queue in the center, and move proof panels below.
Traffic is climbing steadily after content refreshes and title changes.
